stimulus.title: Capillary tubes of different widths
stimulus.text: PLACEHOLDER content, written only to test the free-response pages; it has had no accuracy check. A student stands glass tubes of three inside widths (0.5 mm, 1.0 mm and 2.0 mm) upright in a dish of water and measures how high the water rises inside each tube after one minute.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State a null hypothesis for this investigation.

rubric.point: The width of the tube has no effect on the height the water rises.
accept: no difference in height among the tube widths

parts.sample: The inside width of the tube has no effect on how high the water rises in it.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify one variable the student should keep the same in every tube.

rubric.point: Any valid controlled variable: water temperature, tube material, time before measuring, depth the tube is placed.

parts.sample: The water temperature should be the same for every tube.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Predict which tube will show the highest rise.
parts.sample: The 0.5 mm tube will show the highest rise.

parts.label: d

rubric.point: In a narrow tube, adhesion to the glass acts on a larger share of the water column relative to its weight, and cohesion pulls the rest of the column up with it.
accept: more glass surface per volume of water, so adhesion lifts it higher

parts.sample: Water molecules stick to the glass by adhesion and pull the molecules below them up by cohesion. In a narrow tube there is more glass surface for each unit of water weight, so the water is pulled higher.
